title: Per-endpoint probationary SLO and staged failover orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a probationary SLO lifecycle for newly created per-endpoint or per-model routes combined with a staged regional failover and circuit-breaker orchestration. New routes will start on a short, conservative SLO window (probation) with tighter burn thresholds and increased observability. After sustained stability the route graduates to standard SLOs. During probation and normal operation, we coordinate region-aware circuit breakers and load-shedding priorities so that failover decisions preserve high-value traffic and avoid unnecessary model variant cross-traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Definition and schema for probationary SLO that can be attached to any endpoint via route config
Automated graduation logic: conditions (no high-severity errors, stable latency p95/p99 under defined delta) and manual override path
Circuit-breaker rules that consume per-endpoint error budget and regional saturation signals to decide: degrade->fallthrough->regional-eject
Load-shedding policy that exposes priority buckets (pinned customers, premium routes, best-effort) and ensures pinned traffic is preserved up to defined capacity
Dashboards: probation SLO burn rate, per-region variant health, and failover decision trace for last 72 hours
End-to-end test harness + canary runbook demonstrating failover from us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 with controlled shedding
notes: Rationale: we frequently onboard experimental routes and variants which create noisy SLO signals; probation protects global SLOs while we collect realistic traffic patterns
Probation windows considered: 1h, 6h, 24h. Proposal: default 6h with override per-route
Graduation condition prototype: <1% error budget burn over probation window AND less than 30% increase p99 compared to baseline traffic-matched cohort
Circuit-breaker tiers: soft (reduce concurrency/batch size), hard (reject new requests, fallback to cheaper variant), regional-eject (redirect traffic to other region/model)
decisions: Use a separate probationary error budget ledger to avoid contaminating global error budgets: ledger is a first-class resource tied to route key
Tie circuit-breaker thresholds to both error-budget burn-rate and quantile latency signals (p95/p99) instead of only raw error rate
Implement load-shedding by priority score computed from (customer_tier, route_priority, pinned_flag, recent_error_budget_score)
Failover orchestration will include a 30s cool-off timer before regional-eject to allow transient recoveries and avoid flapping

implementation_notes: Engineer notes: ledger records use tokenized route key and windowed counters. We will add a lightweight admission controller to annotate routes with probation SLO meta. Circuit-breaker will subscribe to kafka topic for regional saturation signals. Load-shedding decisions emitted to route-proxy via x-shed header for stateless evaluation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive probation could mask genuine incidents — mitigation: keep probation window short and expose manual override + human alerting
Risk: Increased complexity in failover logic could introduce flapping — mitigation: cool-off timers and test harness that simulates region jitter
Risk: Pinned customer preservation may starve best-effort traffic under extended outage — mitigation: define absolute capacity floors for best-effort and emergency reclamation policy
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger bookkeeping and burn-rate calc
Integration tests: simulate multi-region latency/packet-loss, assert staged failover sequence
Chaos test: induce region ejection and assert no double-ejections within 5 minute window
Canary: enable probation for synthetic route, drive traffic and validate graduation path
